label: anteriority and posteriority: before and after
note: CLOSED BY CHAPTER 106. THE OLD NOTE WAS HALF RIGHT AND THE DRAFT OF THIS ONE CALLED IT SOUND. 'munpu and shesham are not taught' is true -- neither appears anywhere in the corpus. 'pinne (then) is the nearest and it sequences TURNS rather than EVENTS' is FALSE: ML-C68-at-first (2350) says 'aadyaM puts an ACTION first in TIME, and it pairs with pinne', tables it under 'an action in time', and gives aadyaM uuNu, pinne chaaya -- lunch first, then tea. That orders the world. The note anticipated the domain check in its own sentence and I read that as the check having been done, which is the domain failure one level up. WHAT WAS GENUINELY MISSING, and what chapter 106 supplies, is the ability to fix an event against a NAMED point. aadyaM and pinne lay a run out without saying when any of it happens; munpu and shEshaM take a named hour or event and place something relative to it, which is what anteriority and posteriority means. Both are postpositions on the dative, so raNTu maNikku munpu reuses ML-C102-manikku's form and uuNinu shEshaM shows the dative's other shape on uuNu (930).
